title: Sindhu, Lakshya Make It A Double Delight For India At Hylo Open
indian_angle: Two of India's top shuttlers, PV Sindhu and Lakshya Sen, secured titles at the Hylo Open, marking a significant double victory for the nation.
summary: Former world champion PV Sindhu and Lakshya Sen both triumphed in their respective finals at the Hylo Open in Staarbrucken, Germany, securing a rare Indian badminton double. Sindhu added the Hylo Open to her Japan Open triumph, boosting her World Tour Finals hopes, while Sen ended his title drought in style.

title: BAI Announces Formation Of New Athletes Committee
indian_angle: The Badminton Association of India has officially formed its new Athletes Committee, a crucial step for player representation in national badminton.
summary: The Badminton Association of India (BAI) officially announced the formation of its Athletes Committee on October 2, 2026, aiming to provide a direct channel for players' voices in the sport's governance.

title: National Coaching Camp For BWF World Junior Championships 2026 Begins In Guwahati
indian_angle: India's junior shuttlers are undergoing intensive training at the National Center of Excellence in Guwahati in preparation for the upcoming BWF World Junior Championships.
summary: A national coaching camp for the BWF World Junior Championships 2026 commenced at the National Center of Excellence (NCE) in Guwahati on September 24, 2026, focusing on preparing India's young talent for the global event.

title: BAI Level 1 Advanced Coaches Course Held In Guwahati And Raipur
indian_angle: The Badminton Association of India conducted an advanced Level-1 coaches course across two national centers, enhancing the quality of coaching available to Indian players.
summary: The Badminton Association of India (BAI) hosted a Level-1 (Advanced) Coaches Course at the National Center of Excellence in Guwahati and Raipur from September 14 to 23, 2026, aimed at upskilling national badminton coaches.

title: New 3x15 Scoring System Implemented In Domestic Junior Tournaments
indian_angle: The Badminton Association of India has implemented a new 3x15 scoring system for domestic junior tournaments, which will significantly impact how young Indian players compete.
summary: The Badminton Association of India (BAI) announced the implementation of a 3x15 scoring system for domestic ranking tournaments and National Championships across U-13, U-15, and U-17 age groups, effective June 30, 2026.
